Henderson trend filter with Musgrave end weights

Source: R/smoothers.R
henderson_filter.Rd

Applies a Henderson moving average to a complete series, with the symmetric weights in the interior and the Musgrave asymmetric weights at the first and last p points. The length can be chosen among candidates by generalised cross-validation.

Usage

henderson_filter(x, length = NULL, lengths = c(13L, 23L, 39L), ic_ratio = NULL)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector, complete (no NA) and finite.

length

NULL (choose by GCV among lengths) or a single odd integer >= 3 not longer than x.

lengths

Candidate odd lengths when length = NULL.

ic_ratio

NULL (estimate) or a non-negative I/C ratio for the Musgrave end weights.

Value

A list with trend (numeric, same length as x), length (chosen length), ic_ratio (used), edf (trace of the smoother matrix), gcv (GCV of the chosen length) and path (data.table with length, edf and gcv for every candidate evaluated).

Details

Interior and ends. For a length H = 2p + 1, points p + 1 to n - p get the symmetric weights of henderson_weights(). At the end point with q < p future observations, the Musgrave weights on the M = p + 1 + q available observations are (Doherty 2001) $$u_i = w_i + \frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=M+1}^{N} w_j + \frac{(i - \frac{M+1}{2})\,D}{1 + \frac{M(M-1)(M+1)}{12}D} \sum_{j=M+1}^{N}\left(j - \frac{M+1}{2}\right) w_j,$$ with \(D = 4 / (\pi R^2)\) and R the I/C ratio (mean absolute weekly change of the irregular over that of the trend). The weights sum to one. They minimise the expected revision under a locally linear trend with noise, so they reproduce a straight line exactly only in the limit R -> 0; for R > 0 the slope enters as a penalty, not a constraint. The first p points use the mirrored weights.

I/C ratio. When ic_ratio = NULL, R is estimated from a preliminary 13-term Henderson pass with R = 3.5 (the X-11 value for that length): R = mean(|diff(x - C)|) / mean(|diff(C)|), C the preliminary trend. Series shorter than 13 use the longest odd length that fits. The same R is used for every candidate length.

Length. When length = NULL, each candidate of lengths not longer than the series is applied and the one with the smallest \(GCV = n\,RSS / (n - \mathrm{tr}\,S)^2\) is kept, where S is the linear smoother matrix (symmetric rows in the interior, Musgrave rows at the ends) and \(\mathrm{tr}\,S\) its trace (the equivalent degrees of freedom). GCV assumes independent errors; with positively autocorrelated noise it tends to choose short filters.

Missing values. The filter needs a complete series: x with NA raises an error. Fill missing values first (e.g. linear interpolation, or the fitted values of a previous pass as in X-11).

References

Doherty, M. (2001). The surrogate Henderson filters in X-11. Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics, 43(4), 385-392.

Musgrave, J. C. (1964). A set of end weights to end all end weights. Working paper, U.S. Bureau of the Census.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- sin(seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 120)) + rnorm(120, 0, 0.2)
h <- henderson_filter(x)
h$length
#> [1] 23
h$path
#>    length      edf        gcv
#>     <int>    <num>      <num>
#> 1:     13 29.26902 0.03831919
#> 2:     23 17.79198 0.03671435
#> 3:     39 11.10826 0.03729414
h13 <- henderson_filter(x, length = 13L, ic_ratio = 3.5)
head(h13$trend)
#> [1] 0.005961282 0.104230080 0.220273681 0.339850516 0.454927050 0.557178899
